routes.reason: RP.0 (height machine, canonical heights) and RP.5 (subvarieties of abelian varieties, finite-rank subgroups, Manin–Mumford) are the right homes for the finite-rank notion, the Faltings–Zhang morphism of a single abelian variety, the quartic duplication formulas and Silverman–Tate.

A2 owns Picard functors and polarizations of abelian schemes. It takes Remark 3.1's projective presentation and, with this review, Mumford's projective normality (item 66), on which Serre's quartic formulas depend.

SF.0/SF.5 own the scheme-theoretic and intersection-theoretic foundations: EGA line-bundle descent, Siu's criterion, Fulton positivity, Cartier/Weil divisors, Bézout and quasi-sections. Item 29 is restricted to what the paper uses.
ComplexComparisonPartII C5 is the home of integration of forms over analytic sets and its comparison with intersection numbers.

The Betti map and Betti form, the non-degeneracy criterion and Gao's theorem form the AbelianSchemesBettiMapsPartII, which GAO-HABEGGER-19 and GAO-GE-KUHNE-26 propose under the same id. The Prop 2.7 statement should be proved by the pointwise argument (sourceIssues E14).

The height inequality, the counting in §§7–8 and the main theorems belong to the uniformity Part II shared with YUAN-26, GAO-HABEGGER-19, GAO-GE-KUHNE-26, DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20 and DEMARCO-MAVRAKI-YE-26. Rémond's bound (item 67) is added there.
Moduli of curves with level structure and the Torelli morphism go to YUAN-26's StableReductionPartII; the acceptance criterion is corrected so that τ is injective for g = 2 (sourceIssues E11).
Relative Jacobians of the universal curve go to YUAN-26's JacobianChallengePartII, consistent with Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge (curves over a field) and A2 (Picard for abelian schemes).
